clippings.speaker: Simon Pegg
clippings.quote: We still use a flip chart to lay out all our ideas. We start on a large canvas and then refine and refine until we have the screenplay we want to shoot. We never stop writing, all through the shoot and even through the edit. … I love writing with Edgar, I think we bring out the best in each other.
clippings.title: Simon Pegg Talks THE WORLD'S END, the Film's Soundtrack, Writing with Edgar Wright, and More
clippings.context: Pegg describing how he and Wright co-wrote The World's End, ahead of its release.

clippings.speaker: Simon Pegg
clippings.quote: I try and stay present, so that I'm there for Edgar if he needs me and Edgar won't lock the film until we are both happy.
clippings.title: Simon Pegg Talks THE WORLD'S END, the Film's Soundtrack, Writing with Edgar Wright, and More
clippings.context: Pegg on his role in the edit, which Wright and editor Paul Machliss lead.

clippings.speaker: Simon Pegg
clippings.quote: Well, this one was me and Edgar (Wright). We write in a collaborative way with a brainstorming session, and then brought Nick into the process for his input on the rest of the script. … Edgar has an idea of how the scenes are cut, so there is no need for extra nonsense, money wasted.
clippings.title: Interview: The World's End with Edgar Wright, Simon Pegg & Nick Frost
clippings.context: Pegg, interviewed with Nick Frost on the Australian press tour, on their writing process; the Q&A format does not label speakers, but he refers to writing with Edgar himself.

clippings.speaker: Edgar Wright
clippings.quote: No, I don't think we have really done anything separately on all three films. The only fancy thing that we do now is to plug the laptop into the TV; prior to that, it was like battleships with two laptops opposite each other and one person is typing and the other person is pacing.
clippings.title: Edgar Wright Exclusive Interview
clippings.context: Wright answering whether he and Pegg ever write separately, for the home-video release of The World's End.

clippings.speaker: Edgar Wright
clippings.quote: The characters are an amalgamation of friends that both Simon and I had; there weren't any specific people. … I would say that there are parts of me and Simon in all of the main characters.
clippings.title: Edgar Wright Exclusive Interview
clippings.context: Wright on how the World's End gang was drawn from his and Pegg's own lives.

clippings.speaker: Edgar Wright
clippings.quote: Simon has less body fat after appearing on screen with Tom Cruise (Mission Impossible 3 & 4) inspired him to get ridiculously gym fit, Simon is suddenly ripped. His hair is longer too, he wanted to wear a wig but I insisted he had to dye it.
clippings.title: Interview: The World's End with Edgar Wright, Simon Pegg & Nick Frost
clippings.context: Wright, asked how Pegg and Frost had changed over years of working together, on Pegg's look for Gary King.

notes: IndieWire's Shaun of the Dead oral history redirected to a TollBit paywall and was skipped; Something About Rocks (2026, Pegg calls Wright 'one of my best friends') would not load as raw text, so it was left out. All quotes are from 2013 World's End press.
